claims.text: Atomic size differences in as-cast HfNbTaTiZr create local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions govern the unusual stress–strain and thermoelastic responses of HfNbTaTiZr.
Local lattice distortions induce thermal-expansion mismatches.
Internal mismatch stresses influence high-temperature creep in HfNbTaTiZr.
Internal mismatch stresses influence elastic-modulus variations in HfNbTaTiZr.
Internal mismatch stresses influence microhardness after deformation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Internal mismatch stresses influence age hardening in HfNbTaTiZr.
Partially substituting elements to reduce atomic-size mismatch will reduce lattice distortion while allowing the overall phase structure to remain similar.
Atomic-size disparities produce internal elastic heterogeneity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Heating makes the distorted regions produce local thermal-expansion mismatch and internal stress.
Mismatch-generated internal stresses impede dislocation motion.
Reducing atomic-size mismatch will decrease internal mismatch stresses.
The modified alloy will have a lower tensile-creep rate at 1250 °C than standard HfNbTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will exhibit less age-induced hardening after treatment at 600–800 °C.
The modified alloy's elastic moduli from 293 to 1100 K will more closely follow homogeneous theoretical predictions.
The proposed mechanism operates from 293 K to 1250 °C and is especially influential during aging at 600–800 °C.
Secondary-phase formation and other microstructural heterogeneities may also contribute to the observed behavior.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says mismatch-generated internal stresses impede dislocation motion, which would ordinarily resist creep. The prediction instead says that reducing those stresses will lower the creep rate, without supplying an additional mechanism that reverses the expected direction.
